sections.h2: Where is Quincy and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Quincy is the largest city in Norfolk County, Massachusetts, sitting on Boston Harbor just south of the Neponset River. Wikipedia's Quincy entry lists Boston to the north, Milton to the west, Randolph and Braintree to the south, and Weymouth and Hull across the water to the east.

The city covers 26.9 square miles, but about 37.6 percent of that is water. A large piece of the land is not available for housing at all: the Blue Hills Reservation, a state park, takes up roughly 23 percent of the land area in the southwest corner and holds the city's high point, 517-foot Chickatawbut Hill.

So a Quincy house is usually either on the harbor side, where Quincy Bay and Wollaston Beach shape daily life, or inland on the hills around Quincy Center, South Quincy and West Quincy.

sections.h2: Which Quincy neighborhoods matter when you sell?
sections.html:
Quincy is a city of named neighborhoods, and buyers think in those terms. The main ones, as described on Wikipedia:

  • Wollaston: an early rail commuter area for Boston workers, now dense and mixed residential and commercial.
  • North Quincy: runs along Hancock Street and Quincy Shore Drive and is home to the city's largest high school.
  • Quincy Center: the historic commercial and government core, with City Hall and the Thomas Crane Public Library.
  • Quincy Point: densely settled, east of the center, and the site of the Fore River Shipyard.
  • Houghs Neck and Squantum: peninsulas that began as summer resort areas and are now year-round neighborhoods.
  • Marina Bay: built in the 1980s on the former Naval Air Station Squantum, with high-rise condominiums and a large marina.
  • West Quincy: close to Interstate 93, with the old granite quarries and the Granite Railway site.
  • Merrymount, Montclair, Adams Shore, Germantown and South Quincy: mostly residential, each with its own feel.

A condo at Marina Bay and a single-family house on Houghs Neck are different products with different buyer pools, so the way a sale gets priced and marketed can differ a lot inside one city.

sections.h2: How did Quincy's history shape its housing?
sections.html:
Quincy grew in stages, and its houses tend to show it. Granite quarrying dominated 19th century jobs, and the Granite Railway, built in 1826, is recognized as the first commercial railroad in the United States.

The Old Colony Railroad opened in 1845 and made Quincy about as reachable from Boston as Charlestown. The first suburban land company in the north of the city formed in 1870, and the population grew by more than 50 percent during the 1920s. Shipbuilding at the Fore River Shipyard then carried the 20th century economy.

A city built across that many decades usually has houses of many ages on the same street. That matters for a sale, because wiring, heating, roofs and smoke alarms can differ sharply from one house to the next.

sections.h2: What are the major employers, schools and commutes?
sections.html:
Quincy has moved from heavy industry to office and service work. Wikipedia names Stop & Shop, Arbella Insurance Group, Boston Financial Data Services and The Patriot Ledger as companies headquartered in the city, and lists State Street, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts, Harvard Pilgrim Health Care and Boston Scientific among the larger employers with offices there.

The commute story is strong. The MBTA Red Line has four Quincy stops: North Quincy, Wollaston, Quincy Center and Quincy Adams. Interstate 93 and U.S. 1 run together through the west side, and Route 3A, Route 28 and Route 53 cross the city.

Public schools are run by Quincy Public Schools, with two high schools (Quincy High School and North Quincy High School), five middle schools and a set of elementary schools. Quincy College, in Quincy Center, is unusual because the city itself operates it.

sections.h2: How does Quincy weather affect an older house?
sections.html:
Quincy gets a full New England winter, and that is what inspectors and buyers look at first. NOAA normals for the Blue Hill station put average snowfall at 69.7 inches a year, with about 29 snowy days, and January lows average 18.3 degrees Fahrenheit.

Rain is steady too, at 53.86 inches a year across about 140 days with measurable precipitation. In practice that points a buyer's attention to roofs, gutters, basements and heating systems, and to anything near the water on the Quincy Bay side.

If your house sits close to the shore, ask your insurance agent and the city building department about flood mapping before you list. We did not find a city flood page to cite here, so this page makes no flood claims.

sections.h2: What must a Quincy seller do before closing?
sections.html:
Quincy sellers face the same Massachusetts requirements as everyone else in the state, plus Norfolk County recording charges. The short list:

  • Smoke and CO certificate: The state Department of Fire Services says a seller needs a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing the alarms meet the rules for a sale. Call the Quincy fire department as soon as you have a closing date, because there is an inspection fee.
  • Alarm age: Battery-powered smoke alarms over ten years old, or with no date stamp, must be replaced with sealed ten-year photoelectric units that have a hush feature.
  • Deed excise tax: Norfolk County's registry charges $2.28 for each $500 of the price on the deed. Its own example is a $155,000 deed costing $706.80.

sections.h2: How does Quincy bill property tax?
sections.html:
Quincy bills real estate tax quarterly. According to the Quincy Assessors page, the first two bills are preliminary, together about 50 percent of the prior year's tax, due August 1 and November 1.

The third and fourth bills use the new assessed value and the year's tax rate, with the payments already made subtracted. They are due February 1 and May 1.

Property record cards are posted online, and the assessors say a new valuation shows up on the third-quarter bill each January. The office is at 1305 Hancock Street and its listed phone is (617) 376-1170.

If you think your assessment is too high, state guidance from the Appellate Tax Board says the abatement application is due by the first installment due date, generally February 1 in quarterly cities. Assessors have three months to act, and an appeal to the board follows within three months of their decision. Taxes have to be paid on time for the appeal to stay alive. Ask your closing attorney how the current quarter will be handled at the table.

sections.h2: What do Quincy sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
Sellers in a city like Quincy tend to hit a handful of situations, and each has a practical first step:

  • A house that needs work: get a rough repair list before choosing between listing and a cash sale, so you compare real net numbers.
  • Alarm and certificate timing: book the fire department early so a missed inspection does not delay closing.
  • An inherited house: the estate may need court authority before it can sell, so talk to a probate attorney first.
  • Tight timelines: a job move or a payment problem favors a quick, certain closing over a long marketing period.

Every route, from a standard listing to a cash offer, ends at the same Norfolk County recording step. The difference is how many repairs, showings and weeks you need before you get there.

faqs.a: Quincy covers 26.9 square miles, about 37.6 percent of it water, and had 101,636 residents at the 2020 census.
Yes. Quincy is the largest city in Norfolk County, so deeds for Quincy houses are recorded at the Norfolk Registry of Deeds.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate to sell in Quincy?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing the alarms meet the standards for a sale or transfer. Schedule it as soon as you have a closing date.

faqs.q: How much is the deed excise tax in Quincy?
faqs.a: Norfolk County charges $2.28 for every $500 of the deed's stated price. On a $155,000 deed the registry's example comes to $706.80.

faqs.q: When are Quincy property taxes due?
faqs.a: Quincy bills quarterly, with due dates of August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1, according to the city assessors.
